title: Schedule of Late Fee Percentages for Repeated Lateness — Independent Living
content:
Repeated lateness raises the late fee percentage applied to the past-due amount of a billing period on an Independent Living Residency Agreement account.

## Schedule

Repeated lateness is counted as **the late fees posted on the residency within the 12 months ending on the day of assessment**.

| Late fees posted on the residency within the 12 months | Late fee percentage |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 3.0 percent |
| Exactly one | 2.25 percent |
| None | The late fee percentage of the apartment type's billing schedule, unchanged |

## Notes to the schedule

- The count reads late fee entries already on this residency's ledger whose posting date falls within the 12 months ending on the day of assessment; the window runs back to the day after the same date twelve months earlier.
- A late fee that was later waived by a goodwill credit is still a late fee entry posted on the ledger.
- The percentage selected here is the late fee percentage that is then applied to the past-due amount of the billing period.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- Late fees posted on March 12 and July 12, 2026, and a late fee assessed on December 14, 2026: two late fees in the window, so the late fee percentage is 3.0.
- A single late fee posted on December 13, 2025 and an assessment on December 14, 2026: the earlier fee is outside the 12 months, so no late fee is counted.
- One late fee posted on June 12, 2026 and an assessment on December 14, 2026: the late fee percentage is 2.25.
